newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Over-supply cuts Beijing prime office occupancy.
newsitem.headline: Over-supply cuts Beijing prime office occupancy.

text.p: Prime office occupancy in China's capital Beijing is forecast to decline to around 70 percent in 1998, according to a quarterly report by Asian real estate consultants Marlin Land released on Tuesday.

The report said prime rents were expected to decline in line with occupancy rates by another seven percent by end-1996, by 20 percent in 1997 and 12 percent in 1998, before bottoming out at around US$46 per square metre.
The company's Asian Property Update said the emergence of new grade A office supply since the second half of 1995 had caused occupancy rates and prime rentals to decline.
Average prime rents were now 25 percent down from the peak levels achieved in late 1994, it said.
It said projected growth in the number of foreign companies in Beijing amounted to 20 percent a year, but their take-up of office space would not fully absorb new supply coming up.
